Neither candidate specifically isolates an 'Other Consumer' or overdraft portfolio composition and charge-off performance comparable to BAC's specific disclosure on deposit overdraft balances and fraud-related charge-offs.

comparisons.peer_summary: Provision for credit losses increased to $1.54 billion in 2024 from $1.14 billion in 2023, primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS report net charge-offs driven by consumer credit portfolios, but the specific drivers and magnitude differ significantly. BAC's 'Other Consumer' portfolio, consisting mainly of overdrafts, saw net charge-offs decrease to $295 million, primarily due to lower fraud-related losses. In contrast, GS's credit card portfolio saw net charge-offs drive an increase in credit loss provisions to $1.54 billion, reflecting higher credit costs in that specific consumer lending segment.

comparisons.peer_topic: Auto and other loan portfolio performance
comparisons.peer_summary: The auto and other loan portfolio, consisting mainly of prime-quality auto and business banking loans, decreased from the prior year due to securitizations, while net charge-offs increased to $445 million from $357 million in 2023 due to declining used vehicle valuations.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM disclose performance metrics for 'Other Consumer' or 'Other' loan portfolios that include overdrafts. BAC's Other Consumer portfolio (overdrafts) saw net charge-offs decrease to $295 million, driven by reduced fraud. JPM's 'Auto and other' portfolio, which also includes overdrafts, saw net charge-offs increase to $445 million, driven by declines in used vehicle valuations within its auto loan segment. While both portfolios contain overdrafts, the primary driver of loss variation differs: fraud for BAC and vehicle valuation/auto credit quality for JPM.
